title: Skin-Anderson Localization Transition in Strongly Coupled Disordered Non-Hermitian Chains
abstract: The interplay between disorder and non-Hermitian effects gives rise to a variety of intriguing localization phenomena. While disorder tends to localize the eigenstates through Anderson localization, non-Hermitian non-reciprocity promotes the formation of skin modes by driving the eigenstates toward the system boundaries giving rise to non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). In this work, we investigate the interplay between these competing mechanisms in a two-leg ladder consisting of a Hatano-Nelson chain coupled to a Hermitian chain via asymmetric inter-chain hopping, with strong disorder present in both chains. We show that tuning the asymmetry of the inter-chain coupling induces successive transitions in the nature of the eigenstates, from skin localization to Anderson localization and subsequently back to skin localization. Remarkably, the non-Hermitian skin effect re-emerges even though the energy spectrum exhibits a line-gap topology, demonstrating that robust skin localization can persist beyond the conventional point-gap regime.
summary: This paper explores the competition between disorder (Anderson localization) and non-reciprocity (NHSE) in a two-leg ladder model. By tuning the inter-chain coupling asymmetry, the authors demonstrate successive transitions in eigenstate behavior, showing that robust skin localization can persist even when the energy spectrum topology changes away from conventional point gaps.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex interplay between disorder-induced Anderson localization and non-Hermitian effects, specifically the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE).
main_result: Tuning the asymmetry of inter-chain coupling drives successive transitions in eigenstate nature: from skin localization to Anderson localization, and back to skin localization even when the energy spectrum exhibits a line-gap topology.
method: The analysis involves calculating the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR) and Mean Center of Mass ($	ext{mcom}$) averaged over disorder realizations to diagnose the spatial extent and localization type of eigenstates.
model_or_system: The model is a two-leg ladder system comprising a Hatano–Nelson chain coupled to a Hermitian chain via asymmetric inter-chain hopping. The Hamiltonian incorporates onsite disorder terms ($\Delta_j$) and coupling parameters ($t, a$).

important_parameters: The asymmetry parameter '$a$' is the primary control, which tunes the competition between localization mechanisms; critical points include $a=0$, $a=t$, and $a>t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating the system as a tight-binding model with disorder, focusing on the spectral and spatial properties of eigenstates.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes how varying the inter-chain asymmetry parameter '$a$' drives successive phase transitions in localization, mapping out regimes where NHSE dominates versus where disorder-induced Anderson localization prevails.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how competing non-Hermitian and random potentials dictate fundamental transport properties like localization, which has implications for designing robust quantum devices.
